docs.title: Expose Prometheus metrics from a service
docs.text: This recipe shows how the metrics exposed by the service can be scraped by Prometheus and displayed in Grafana deployed inside a Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Deploy the Prometheus stack
docs.text:
$ kubectl create namespace monitoring
$ helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
$ helm install prom prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack --version 92.17.1 -n monitoring
# Wait until all pods become ready
$ helm test prom -n monitoring
# Get the login password for Grafana
$ kubectl get secret prom-grafana -n monitoring -o jsonpath="{.data.admin-password}" | base64 --decode; echo
# Make Grafana accessible over localhost:3000
$ kubectl port-forward service/prom-grafana -n monitoring 3000:80
  • Open http://localhost:3000/
  • Login with admin and the password read from the secret previously

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text:
$ docker build -t ghcr.io/bszendro/videoservice/videoservice:1.0.0 .
# Login the first time
$ docker login ghcr.io -u bszendro
$ docker push ghcr.io/bszendro/videoservice/videoservice:1.0.0

docs.title: Deploy the image using Helm
docs.text:
NOTE: When using a private repository on GHCR, create a Personal access token (classic) on GitHub with write:packages permissions, then store the secret in k8s. (Note that this secret is not encrypted in the DB by default.) ```bash $ kubectl create secret docker-registry ghcr-access-key --docker-server=ghcr.io --docker-username=bszendro --docker-password=

$ kubectl get secret ghcr-access-key ``` 

$ helm install vidserv ./vidserv --version 1.0.0
# Wait until all pods become ready
$ helm test vidserv

The metrics exposed by the service pods should be visible in Grafana's Explore view now. The way this works is that the Prometheus stack operator detects the PodMonitor resource created by Helm when deploying the service. The PodMonitor resource in the chart has a release label that matches the selector value in the Prometheus resource:

# Check what podmonitors will this Prometheus instance use
$ kubectl get prometheus prom-kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus -n monitoring -o json | jq '.spec.podMonitorSelector.matchLabels'
{
  "release": "prom"
}
